hints: Start with Q at the pointed bottom tip (apex) of the heart and P as the small dark ear-like flap at the top, both are chambers, so think which side forms the apex in a front view.

Look at R as a blood vessel running on the outside surface of the muscle, and S as a large thin-walled vessel entering the top, recall which vessels are visible externally versus conducting tissues hidden inside.
walkthrough:
**Get your orientation for a front view**

Think of looking at someone facing you. Their left is on your right. The big thick pointed tip at the bottom, labelled Q, is the apex. That is almost always the left ventricle because it does the hardest pumping work.

**Identify the two chambers P and Q**

P is the small wrinkled flap (auricle) at the top edge. In a front view this is the left atrium peeking out. Q is the thick muscular wall at the apex, which is the left ventricle. This already points to row B.

**Check the vessels R and S to confirm**

R is a vessel branching over the outer surface of the ventricle wall. That is the position of a coronary artery supplying cardiac muscle, not Purkyne tissue which is hidden deep inside the walls. S is a large vessel entering the top of the right side, the position of the vena cava returning blood to the right atrium.

options.A: P and Q positions are partly right, but R is a coronary artery on the surface, not Purkyne tissue which is internal, and S is the vena cava, not the pulmonary vein.
options.B: P is the left atrium auricle, Q is the muscular left ventricle at the apex, R is the coronary artery on the surface, and S is the vena cava entering at the top. All four match the front view.
options.C: P is on the left side, not the right atrium, and R is an external coronary artery, not internal Purkyne tissue, and S is not the thick-walled aorta.
options.D: Q at the apex is the left ventricle, not the right ventricle which is more anterior and less pointed, and P is left atrium and S is vena cava, not as stated.
